title: RunEvent
description: The normalized event every producer's wire event maps into and every consumer folds.

coordinator_job_id.description:
The coordinator's Batch job id, set only on `coordinator_submitted` (always equal to its
`batch_job_id`). Informational: the fold joins on `batch_job_id`, and nothing in biffix
reads this back. It stays a published contract field because stored events carry it and
external consumers may name the coordinator by it (additive-only).

dedup_key.description: Producer-computed, deterministic; the log dedupes on it.

queue.description:
The AWS Batch job queue (its name, not ARN) an `aws-batch` event's job ran on. Like
`instance_id`, a fact about where the attempt ran; it tells a spot attempt from an on-demand
one when the host's own lifecycle is unknown.

requested_memory_mib.description:
The memory (MiB) an `aws-batch` event's job asked Batch for (its `MEMORY` resource
requirement). As `requested_vcpus`.

requested_vcpus.description:
The vCPUs an `aws-batch` event's job asked Batch for (its `VCPU` resource requirement): what
the attempt requested, not what its host has. Like `queue`, a fact about the attempt,
carried by the Batch state-change events that name it (not by a reaped terminal, which has
no container); the reducer keeps the minimum across the events that carry it. `f64` end to
end (wire, column, API), so a fractional request reads back exactly. Optional + additive:
absent on events from before this field and on jobs whose event names no requirement.

oneOf.description: The control plane accepted the run — its provenance anchor (see [`RunSubmitted`]).

session_id.description:
The engine's own session id, reported by the engine plugin at start (Nextflow
`session.uniqueId`). A cross-check on the anchor's `engine_session_id`; `None` from the
Snakemake logger and on events from before this field existed.

reason.description:
Why the control plane failed the run before it launched (e.g. a submit-time image that
could not be prepared). `None` from the engine, and on events from before this field
existed. Optional + additive.

stage.description:
Which step of the control plane failed it: an open vocabulary (see
[`FAILURE_STAGE_IMAGE_PREPARATION`], [`FAILURE_STAGE_LAUNCH`]); a reader treats a value
it does not know, or none, as a launch failure. `None` from the engine, and on events
from before this field existed. Optional + additive.

actor_label.description:
A human label for the actor (email/name), snapshotted when the cancel was asked for, as
a run's anchor snapshots its submitter's. `None` when none was known, and on events
from before this field existed. Optional + additive.

oneOf.description:
The run's intermediate files (a Nextflow run's `work/`) were deleted by the retention sweep;
its results are kept, but it can no longer be resumed.

The run was accepted but waits for its submit-time images before it launches (see
[`RunPreparing`]). Boxed like the anchor it precedes.

The run was put in an experiment (`experiment_id`), moved to another, or taken out of one
(`None`). The latest by `(ts, seq)` wins (see `RunProjection::experiment_id`); it overrides
the experiment the anchor was launched into.

actor.description: Who made the change (the actor id `authorize` returned). Optional + additive.

oneOf.description:
The run was given a new human name (`run_name`), or its name was cleared (`None`: readers
fall back to a derived one). The latest by `(ts, seq)` wins and overrides the name it was
launched with (see `RunProjection::run_name`).

actor.description: Who renamed it (the actor id `authorize` returned). Optional + additive.

oneOf.description:
The coordinator job stopped without succeeding. Batch's account of why (as on
[`EventData::TaskFailed`]) is what the run's failure summary has to go on when the engine
never started or wrote no log (an image that could not be pulled, a lost host, an
out-of-memory kill). Each is optional + additive: absent when Batch reported none.

termination_category.description: How a task attempt ended (open enum).

oneOf.description:
The run's group-level dependency graph (rule graph for Snakemake, process graph for
Nextflow), emitted when the engine knows it. Folds as a set-union so re-emission or
out-of-order delivery converges: its dedup key carries a hash of the node and
edge sets, so a redelivery of the same graph dedupes while a grown or changed graph is a
distinct fact that reaches the fold. Group-level, not per-task-instance — the graph people
read.

deps.description:
The task keys this task depends on in this run: the tasks that produced its inputs.
Additive; empty on events from before this field existed and for a task with no
in-run upstream.

group.description:
The graph node (rule/process) this task instance belongs to, for rolling task states up
onto the DAG. Optional + additive; `None` on events from before this field existed.

image.description:
The container image the attempt's Batch job runs, as the engine resolved it (the
tenant's copy: `<registry>/<repo>@sha256:…`, or a tag when the engine has no digest).
Per-task image provenance for a multi-image run. Optional + additive: `None` from a
plugin that predates it, and on events from before this field existed.

log_stream.description:
The attempt's CloudWatch log stream, from the Batch terminal (the final container's, so
an attempt seen only through its terminal still has its log). `None` for an
engine-reported local-rule terminal and on events from before this field existed.
Optional + additive.

oneOf.description:
A task was satisfied from the engine's cache — it produced its outputs on a prior run and
was never submitted to Batch. Folds to a SUCCEEDED terminal (it counts as done) but is
flagged `cached` on the projection, because a cache-hit never became a Batch job and so must not be
counted as work run this time (cost/runtime views). Engine-reported; carries no exit code.

termination_category.description: How a task attempt ended (open enum).

oneOf.description:
The engine's verdict on one attempt of a task (`task_key` + `attempt` in the correlation
fields), reported by the engine plugin. A `failed` verdict outranks AWS Batch's `SUCCEEDED`
for the *task*: the attempt no longer counts as the task's success (so the task fails, or,
with a retry announced, waits for the retry), while the attempt itself keeps its AWS facts
(state, exit code, host, log stream). With no `attempt`, it applies to every attempt
submitted at or before its `ts`. It changes nothing for a task with no Batch attempt (a
local task's terminal is its engine `task_failed`), and an unknown verdict folds to nothing.
Named in the engine namespace (`engine_*`), so an older backend stores it unfolded.

category.description:
Why, as a category ([`TerminationCategory::MissingOutput`] for missing outputs,
[`TerminationCategory::AppError`] for a rejected exit status). Optional.

reason.description: The engine's own explanation, for display. Optional.

verdict.description: The workflow engine's verdict on a task attempt (open enum).

oneOf.description:
The outputs of one task attempt (or, with no task key, run-level outputs), as a set. Folds
as a union keyed on `s3_uri`, so a re-emission, a partial batch or out-of-order delivery
converges. The task key and attempt ride in the RunEvent correlation fields.

reused.description: True when the outputs were satisfied from the engine cache, not produced by this run.

role.description: The engine's role for every ref in this batch. `None` ⇒ [`OutputRole::Output`].

oneOf.description: biffix started a CodeBuild build (the control plane, right after `StartBuild`).

request.description: What was asked for (the recipe, the inputs), for the record.

outputs.description: The buildspec's exported variables: what the build produced (a digest, …).

reason.description:
The build's final status (`FAILED`, `STOPPED`, `TIMED_OUT`, `FAULT`) and, when known,
the failed phase's message.

oneOf.description:
An unknown kind — preserved verbatim, stored + audited but not folded. The translators
write it as `{"kind": <tag>, "raw": <the wire event>}` ([`EventData::unknown`]), so the
stored kind is never empty and the wire event's own `ts`/`schema_version`/… cannot collide
with the RunEvent envelope's. Being serde's untagged fallback, it also captures a *known*
kind with a malformed payload (see the module doc and
[`EventData::is_degraded_known_kind`]).

Attempt.description: 1-based attempt counter distinguishing retries of a single `task_key`.

BatchJobId.description: AWS Batch job id for a single attempt; the join key between the engine and AWS streams.

CoordinatorJobId.description: The coordinator (head job) Batch job id.

Dag.description:
A run's group-level dependency graph. Carried by [`EventData::RunDag`]; the reducer folds nodes
and edges as set-unions, so the projected graph is a pure function of the observed event set.

DagEdge.description: A directed dependency edge `from → to` between two graph nodes.

DagNode.description: A node in a run's group-level dependency graph (a Snakemake rule or a Nextflow process).

InputTable.description: A samplesheet biffix wrote for a run (see `RunSubmitted::input_tables`).

OutputRef.description: One output object a task wrote (or, for a cached task, was satisfied by).

path.description:
The engine's own name for the file (e.g. a Nextflow publish target relative to its publish
dir), for display. Optional; the backend derives one from `s3_uri` and the run's output
prefix when absent.

ReferenceUse.description:
The reference bundle a run was launched with (see `RunSubmitted::reference_bundle`): its id and
the URIs it filled, by bundle key, as they were at submit.

ReusedSample.description: One sample as the run a resumed run resumes left it ([`SampleSpec::reused`]).

steps.description: Its finished per-sample steps there, by group, with how many tasks each had.

RunId.description: biffix-minted run identifier. Nullable on the wire until attribution.

RunPreparing.description:
The `run_preparing` payload: a run accepted at submit that waits for its submit-time images
before it launches. The provisional facts the run list and page need until the
`run_submitted` anchor (recorded at launch) supersedes them. `params` are redacted.

experiment_id.description:
The experiment the run was launched into, as the anchor will record it. Optional +
additive.

images.description: The submit-time images the run waits for, as pinned.

RunSubmitted.description:
The `run_submitted` anchor's payload — the run's provenance. A named struct so the
control plane builds it with struct-update syntax from [`RunSubmitted::new`] (the required
fields) instead of patching a variant's `None`s after the fact.

Every field after `input_uris` is optional + additive: absent on anchors recorded
before it existed.

dropped_inactive.description:
Params the submit dropped because their `show_if` conditions hid them (the form's
active set), so the record shows what was given but not used. Optional + additive.

engine_session_id.description:
The engine session this run executes as. Nextflow: the session uuid biffix minted (a
fresh run) or re-used (a resumed run) — the key under `<output_prefix>.nextflow/cache/`.
Optional + additive: `None` for Snakemake, and on anchors from before this
field existed.

experiment_id.description:
The experiment the run was launched into (`RunSubmitRequest.experiment`); a later
`experiment_set` moves it. Optional + additive: `None` when launched into none, and on
anchors from before experiments.

image_map.description:
The run's image map: each declared image reference (as written and normalized) to the
tenant image its tasks ran (`images.json`). Optional + additive.

image_source_digest.description:
The digest of the default image as imported, when the run's tasks ran an image derived
from it (a Snakemake image with the version's engine runtime added); `image_digest` is
then the derived image's. Optional + additive.

input_provenance.description:
Per-URI provenance tag (S3 `version-id`, else `ETag`, else empty) captured at the
submit-time existence check, keyed by `input_uris` entry. Optional + additive,
like `submitter`: `None` on events from before this field existed, or for a
producer that has no tag to record (e.g. a prefix input has no ETag).

input_tables.description:
Samplesheets biffix wrote for this run from rows given at submit, by param: where each
was written and its rows, so the run can be re-run with the same samples. Optional +
additive.

output_prefix.description:
The effective output prefix the workflow's outputs land under (the engine's default
storage prefix), captured at submit: a submit-time `--output-prefix`, else the isolated
per-run `s3://<bucket>/biffix/runs/<run_id>/`. Recorded so the run's output location is
a fact of the log, not re-derived (which is wrong for an overridden prefix). Optional +
additive: `None` on events from before this field existed.

reference_bundle.description:
The reference bundle chosen at submit and the URIs it filled (a bundle can be edited
later, so the run keeps what it used). Optional + additive.

resumed_from.description:
The run this one resumes (`--resume-from`): it shares that run's output prefix, work dir
and engine session. Optional + additive: `None` for a fresh run.

retention.description:
What happens to the run's intermediate files once it ends (see [`Retention`]). Absent ⇒
the deploy's default. Optional + additive.

run_name.description:
The run's human name, given at submit (the UI pre-fills it from the workflow's
template). Optional + additive: `None` when the submitter gave none.

runtime.description:
The engine runtime the run's coordinator ran with (see [`RuntimeUse`]). Optional +
additive: `None` on anchors from before pinned engine runtimes.

sample_count.description:
How many samples the run was launched with: those of the samplesheet biffix wrote for it
from rows (the first, when there are several), else of the samplesheet given as an `s3://`
file when submit could read its sample ids (at most 1 MiB, in storage the run may read).
Absent when neither applies. Optional + additive.

samples.description:
The run's samples and the version's hint for matching tasks to them (the Lab view's
per-sample progress; see [`crate::sample_progress`]). Optional + additive: `None` on
anchors from before the field, which then match tasks by the default rules alone.

submit_images.description:
The images given at submit (`--image`), as pinned; their keys are in `image_map`, where
they win over a version image spelled the same. Optional + additive: `None` when the
submit named none, and on anchors from before submit-time images.

submitter.description:
Who/what triggered the run: `user:<id>` or `watcher:<id>`. Optional + additive.
None ⇒ unknown.

submitter_label.description:
A human label for the submitter (email/display name captured from the auth context at
submit). Optional + additive; `None` when unknown (e.g. a watcher, or no email claim).

target.description:
The effective target built for this run (engine-agnostic: a Snakemake target
rule/output, or a Nextflow `-entry` workflow), captured at submit. A submit-time
`--target` overrides the version's registered target; this records whichever was used,
so two runs of one version that build different targets are distinguishable. Optional +
additive: `None` on events from before this field existed, or when neither
the submit nor the version set a target.

RuntimeUse.description:
The engine a run was launched with (see `RunSubmitted::runtime`): the version's pinned release,
the runtime built for it, and the exact coordinator image (base image + that runtime) it ran on.

SampleHint.description:
The author's hint for attributing tasks to samples (`samples:` in `biffix.yaml`), frozen with
the version's form. Every key is optional; without one the default rules apply.

labels.description: Display names for steps, e.g. `STAR_ALIGN: "Align (STAR)"`, named as in `steps`.

steps.description:
Steps forced to one scope, e.g. `joint_call: study`. A step is named by its full group name
or, for a Nextflow process path, its last `:`-separated part (`STAR_ALIGN` names
`NFCORE_RNASEQ:RNASEQ:STAR_ALIGN`); the full name wins when both are given.

additionalProperties.description: Whether a step runs once per sample or once for the whole study (open enum).

tag.description:
Nextflow: a regex over the task's tag whose `sample` group is the sample id. Trusted as
given (its match is the sample even when the sheet does not list it), and it overrides the
default rules, file-name tags included.

wildcard.description:
Snakemake: the wildcard that names the sample. Trusted as given: its value is the sample
even when the run's sheet does not list it.

SampleSpec.description:
What a run knows about its samples, captured at submit (`RunSubmitted::samples`): the sample
ids of the samplesheet biffix wrote from rows, else of the samplesheet given as an `s3://` file
when submit could read them (at most 1 MiB, in storage the run may read); and the version's
hint. `ids` is empty when neither applies: the set is then open, and a sample is whatever a
task key names.

reused.description:
A resumed run's samples as the run it resumes left them: each sample's finished per-sample
steps there ([`SampleGrid::reused_by_resume`] of that run's grid, captured at submit). The
grid shows them as reused where this run has no task of its own (a Snakemake resume creates
no task for a finished step, so without these a sample it skipped entirely would vanish).
Carried on the anchor rather than read from the other run at fold time, so the grid stays a
function of this run's own log. Optional + additive: empty for a run that resumes nothing.

SubmitImage.description:
An image given at submit, pinned: the reference as the submitter wrote it, the digest-pinned
source it was resolved to, and the content key its import is built under.

TaskKey.description:
Stable logical-task identity: Snakemake `rule:sorted(wildcards)` / Nextflow the task name,
`process (index)` untagged and `process (tag) #<index>` tagged (a tag need not be unique;
the index is, and depends on no other task: nf-biffix `BiffixObserver.taskKey`).
Survives retries — all attempts of one rule/process share it.
